communicates.speaker: character_reginald_musgrave
communicates.content: "You probably heard of my poor father's death," said he; "he was carried off about two years ago. Since then I have of course had the Hurlstone estates to manage, and as I am member for my district as well, my life has been a busy one."

events.label: Musgrave asks Holmes whether he is turning his powers to practical ends and Holmes replies he has taken to living by his wits

communicates.speaker: character_reginald_musgrave
communicates.content: "We have had some very strange doings at Hurlstone, and the police have been able to throw no light upon the matter. It is really the most extraordinary and inexplicable business."

events.label: Holmes requests details of the Musgrave incident from Musgrave

communicates.speaker: character_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: "Pray, let me have the details," I cried.

events.label: Musgrave reports that Rachel Howells recovered from illness and is pale and wan

communicates.speaker: character_reginald_musgrave
communicates.content: "So!" said I. "This is how you repay the trust which we have reposed in you. You will leave my service to-morrow."

events.label: Brunton is seen retreating past Musgrave after being confronted
Musgrave examines the bureau and views the paper left behind as a copy of questions and answers in the Musgrave Ritual
Musgrave re-locks the bureau using the key Brunton left
Brunton pleads not to be driven out and offers to give notice and leave in a month

communicates.speaker: character_brunton_butler
communicates.content: "Mr. Musgrave, sir," he cried, in a voice which was hoarse with emotion, "I can't bear disgrace, sir. I've always been proud above my station in life, and disgrace would kill me. My blood will be on your head, sir—it will, indeed—if you drive me to despair. If you cannot keep me after what has passed, then for God's sake let me give you notice and leave in a month, as if of my own free will. I could stand that, Mr. Musgrave, but not to be cast out before all the folk that I know so well."

events.label: Musgrave reduces Brunton's leaving time from a month request to one week

communicates.speaker: character_reginald_musgrave
communicates.content: "You don't deserve much consideration, Brunton," I answered. "Your conduct has been most infamous. However, as you have been a long time in the family, I have no wish to bring public disgrace upon you. A month, however is too long. Take yourself away in a week, and give what reason you like for going." "Only a week, sir?" he cried, in a despairing voice. "A fortnight—say at least a fortnight!" "A week," I repeated, "and you may consider yourself to have been very leniently dealt with."
